correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly constructs the group-ring transport, invertible Fourier transform under the nonmodular assumption, and both forward/backward finite-field Frobenius descent. Nonzero support must be invariant under both invertible character maps and Frobenius, so it is a union of joint orbits. On each selected orbit, multiplicative Fourier coordinates are a cyclic exponent vector; Smith diagonalization over Z/N counts the exact kernel. Zero-orbit choices and trivial-character augmentation factor are independent. The midpoint closed formula is obtained by doubling cycles and Frobenius return. Direct finite tests reproduce 14 cyclic prime-field cases, a genuinely nonscalar two-generator case, and two field-extension cases; no finite test is substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: A natural complete algebraic classification: idempotents of every semisimple connected Alexander quandle algebra over an arbitrary finite field, not merely one small quandle or integral basis elements. The orbit-lattice method replaces nonlinear q^|G| searches by explicit finite integer Smith matrices and distinguishes nonsplitting Frobenius arithmetic. It shows a structural 12-to-32 jump between two Latin Alexander operations on five group elements over F_2, and a uniform 2^|G| midpoint law in characteristic two. These facts affect the full idempotent set, its augmentation split and the study of quandle-ring structures and representations, not an arbitrary slice.
